options: A schedule of what to publish, when and where
A report of what was published, when and where
A list of content ideas without dates or channels
A schedule of when each team member posts
content_creation_tools-1.explanation: A schedule of what content will be published, when and on which channel.

content_creation_tools-2.stem: Which tool is commonly used to edit short videos for TikTok and Reels on a phone?
options: CapCut
Excel
Postman
AutoCAD

content_creation_tools-3.stem: Why use a social media scheduling tool such as Metricool or Buffer-like platforms?
options: To plan, publish and track across channels
To publish on each channel at the same moment
To create the posts and their designs automatically
To reply to every comment on each channel automatically
content_creation_tools-3.explanation: To plan and publish posts across channels at the best times and track performance in one place.

content_creation_tools-4.stem: A short video loses most viewers in the first three seconds. What should be improved?
options: The opening hook
The length of the end credits
The file name of the video
The size of the logo in the corner
content_creation_tools-4.explanation: The hook: the opening seconds must show value or curiosity immediately.

content_creation_tools-5.stem: Which metric best shows whether content builds an audience rather than just reaching people once?
options: Follower growth with repeat engagement and shares
The impressions a post gets within a single day
The total number of posts published each week
The file size of the images used in each post
content_creation_tools-5.explanation: Follower growth and repeat engagement or saves and shares, not reach alone.

options: The share of visitors who complete the desired action
The total number of visitors who reach the site in a month
The cost spent to acquire one single visitor
The average time a visitor spends on one page
conversion_optimization-1.explanation: The share of visitors who complete a desired action.

options: Showing two versions to random halves of the audience
Showing two versions to the audience one week after another
Showing one version to new visitors and one to returning ones
Showing two versions to a panel and asking which is better
conversion_optimization-2.explanation: Showing two versions to randomly split audiences to see which performs better.

conversion_optimization-3.stem: A test is stopped after one day because variant B is ahead. What is the problem?
options: Stopping early inflates the risk of a false result
One day is the standard length for each test
Variant B should usually be declared the winner at once
Tests should be run on weekends alone
conversion_optimization-3.explanation: Stopping early (peeking) inflates false positives; decide sample size and duration in advance.

conversion_optimization-4.stem: What does the ICE scoring framework rank experiment ideas by?
options: Impact, confidence, ease
Income, cost and effort
Interest, clicks and engagement
Idea, channel and execution

conversion_optimization-5.stem: Heatmaps show that visitors never scroll to the call-to-action button. What should you test?
options: Moving the call to action higher on the page
Making the button grey so that it is less visible
Adding more text above the button
Removing the heatmap tool from the site altogether
conversion_optimization-5.explanation: Move the call to action above the fold or make the page shorter, then A/B test it.

email_marketing_automation-1.stem: What is a welcome flow in marketing automation?
options: Automated emails triggered by a new signup
A one-time email sent by hand to each new subscriber
An automated email series sent to all subscribers monthly
An automated discount shown on the website to new visitors
email_marketing_automation-1.explanation: An automated series of emails triggered when someone subscribes.

email_marketing_automation-2.stem: Which metric tells you what share of recipients opened an email?
options: Open rate
Bounce rate
Click-to-open rate
Unsubscribe rate
Relevant messages to groups raise engagement
Fewer messages to the list lower the sending cost
Identical messages to everyone keep the brand consistent
Messages to small groups avoid spam filters entirely
email_marketing_automation-3.explanation: Relevant messages to specific groups raise engagement and reduce unsubscribes.

email_marketing_automation-4.stem: What does a hard bounce mean?
options: The address is permanently invalid and should be removed
The recipient's inbox was full for a short time only
The recipient marked the email as an important message
The email was opened in a mail app on a phone
email_marketing_automation-4.explanation: The address is permanently invalid, so it should be removed from the list.

email_marketing_automation-5.stem: Which practice most improves email deliverability?
options: Authenticate with SPF, DKIM and DMARC
Send from a new domain each month to avoid filters
Send at the same hour each day to the whole list
Add more links and images to look professional
email_marketing_automation-5.explanation: Authenticate the domain (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and keep a clean, engaged list.

marketplace_ecommerce-1.stem: Which of these is an Indonesian e-commerce marketplace?
options: Tokopedia
Notion
Trello
Zoom

marketplace_ecommerce-2.stem: Which element of a product listing most affects search ranking and click-through?
options: A keyword-rich title and strong main image
The date the seller first joined the platform
The colour of the shop banner chosen by the seller
The total number of products sold in the whole shop
marketplace_ecommerce-2.explanation: A keyword-rich, clear title with a strong main image.

marketplace_ecommerce-3.stem: In marketplace ads, ROAS is calculated as...
options: Ad revenue / ad spend
Ad spend divided by ad revenue
Clicks divided by impressions
Profit minus the shipping cost
marketplace_ecommerce-3.explanation: Revenue from ads divided by ad spend.

marketplace_ecommerce-4.stem: A product has high views but a low conversion rate. What should you check first?
options: Price, reviews, photos and description
Ad budget, keywords and the number of views
Shipping options and the delivery partner
Store followers and the number of products listed
marketplace_ecommerce-4.explanation: Price, reviews, photos and description: the listing quality and offer.

marketplace_ecommerce-5.stem: A flash sale sells out in an hour and the seller cancels many orders. What is the main marketplace risk?
options: Poor seller metrics that lower ranking and account standing
Lower visibility only for the products that were cancelled
Higher commission fees on the next flash sale campaign
Refund costs for the orders, with no effect on ranking
marketplace_ecommerce-5.explanation: Cancellations and late shipments hurt seller metrics, ranking and account standing.

search_ads-1.stem: In Google Ads search campaigns, what does CPC mean?
options: Cost per click
Cost per contact
Clicks per cost
Clicks per customer
search_ads-1.explanation: Cost per click: what you pay each time someone clicks your ad.

options: A word that stops ads showing for irrelevant searches
A word that lowers the bid for irrelevant searches
A word that the platform marks as low quality
A word that competitors bid on against your brand
search_ads-2.explanation: A word that stops your ad from showing for irrelevant searches.

search_ads-3.stem: Which factors make up Quality Score?
options: Expected CTR, ad relevance and landing page experience
Bid amount, daily budget and number of keywords
Impressions, reach and frequency
Device type, location and time of day
search_ads-3.explanation: Expected click-through rate, ad relevance and landing page experience.

search_ads-4.stem: CTR is 5% and a campaign gets 2,000 clicks. How many impressions did it get?

search_ads-5.stem: A campaign spends its whole daily budget by noon and misses afternoon buyers. What is the best first step?
options: Adjust budget, bids and ad schedule to spread the spend
Add more broad keywords to reach more buyers
Pause the campaign for a whole week and wait for results
Move all the ads to the cheaper display network
search_ads-5.explanation: Adjust the budget, bids and ad schedule or targeting so spend is spread across the high-converting hours.

seo-1.stem: What does SEO aim to increase?
options: Organic traffic from search engines
Paid clicks coming from advertisements on other sites
Followers on social media
Subscribers to an email list

seo-2.stem: Which free Google tool shows the queries that bring users to your site and its indexing problems?
options: Google Search Console
Google Ads Editor
Google Forms
Google Drive

seo-3.stem: Which is an on-page SEO factor?
options: A title tag that matches the search intent
The number of followers on the brand's Instagram account
The advertising budget of the month
The colour of the logo
seo-3.explanation: Title tags, headings and content that match the search intent.

options: A link from another site to yours
A link from your page to your homepage
A saved copy of your page
A redirect from the http to the https version
seo-4.explanation: A link from another website to yours; quality links are a ranking signal.

seo-5.stem: Two pages target the same keyword and compete in the results. What is this called and what is a typical fix?
options: Cannibalisation, fixed by merging or differentiating the pages
Duplicate ads, fixed by raising the bid on the keyword
Link rot, fixed by deleting all old links at once
Crawl budget, fixed by adding more images to each page
seo-5.explanation: Keyword cannibalisation; merge the pages or differentiate their intent and use canonical tags.

social_media_ads-1.stem: Which tool is used to create and manage Facebook and Instagram ads?
options: Meta Ads Manager
Google Search Console
Canva Presentations
Shopee Seller Centre

social_media_ads-2.stem: What is the Meta Pixel used for?
options: Tracking actions on your website to measure ads
Resizing images so they fit the feed layout
Scheduling posts to publish at a set time
Moderating comments that arrive on the business page
social_media_ads-2.explanation: Tracking visitor actions on your website to measure and optimise ads.

options: People similar to your existing customers
People who already bought twice
People who follow your competitors
People who live in your city
social_media_ads-3.explanation: People who resemble your existing customers, built from a seed audience.

social_media_ads-4.stem: Which campaign objective fits a goal of selling products from a catalogue?
options: Sales
Awareness
Traffic
Leads

social_media_ads-5.stem: An ad's click-through rate falls while frequency rises over weeks. What is the likely cause and fix?
options: Ad fatigue, fixed by new creatives and wider reach
Ad fatigue, fixed by raising the frequency cap further
Audience overlap, fixed by narrowing to one interest
A tracking error, fixed by resetting the conversion pixel
social_media_ads-5.explanation: Ad fatigue; refresh creatives and widen or rotate the audience.

web_analytics-1.stem: In GA4, what is the basic unit of measurement?
options: Events
Pageviews alone
Sessions alone
Hits
Tag links so traffic is attributed to a campaign
Speed up the loading of pages a campaign links to
Encrypt shared links so other people cannot read them
Shorten links so they fit in social media posts
web_analytics-2.explanation: They tag links so analytics can attribute traffic to a source, medium and campaign.

web_analytics-3.stem: What is Google Tag Manager used for?
options: Managing tracking tags without editing the site code
Designing the layout of landing pages for new ad campaigns
Buying ad space on partner sites relevant to the product
Storing customer data in the company's own database
web_analytics-3.explanation: Managing tracking tags on a site without editing code each time.

web_analytics-4.stem: A funnel shows 10,000 visitors, 3,000 add to cart, 1,500 start checkout and 1,200 buy. Which step has the biggest relative drop?
options: Visit to add-to-cart, with a 70% loss
Cart to checkout, with a 50% loss
Checkout to purchase, with a 20% loss of buyers
There is no drop at some step
web_analytics-4.explanation: Visit to add-to-cart loses 70%; cart to checkout loses 50%; checkout to purchase loses 20%.

web_analytics-5.stem: Last-click attribution gives all the credit to the final touchpoint. What is a weakness?
options: It undervalues the earlier touchpoints that started the journey
It counts every purchase twice in the final campaign report
It cannot be used together with any paid ad campaign
It needs a formal signed contract with the ad platform
web_analytics-5.explanation: It undervalues earlier touchpoints such as awareness campaigns that started the journey.
